By the fourth buoy she had found 423 that read the same pressure, 82 that disagreed with each other, and 12 that pointed stubbornly at "fair" while rain came through the awning. She wrote the tally on the back of a customs form stamped 30d50430 and noted beneath it that the remaining 437 had not been opened, since the hinges were rusted shut and the captain wanted his crowbar back. At the 17th mile the fog lifted long enough to show a lighthouse no chart admitted to, painted the green of old copper, with its lamp turning the wrong way. She added that to the form as well, under "discrepancies," and signed it e291.

The numbers and stamps (46, 7:35, 954, 423, 82, 12, 17, 30d50430, e291, even "Afc") come straight from those session strings. Two instances could only collide if they had the same IDs and made the same choices around them.
